# PR-4a — authorized server-side Task history, search and cursor pagination

**Status:** DESIGN ONLY · Draft; base `21b62a2c7fd6ce4862d05cf88fbdd111ac0af6d4`. **Owner:** server TaskStore/query projection + dashboard frontend.

## Existing behavior and core defect
`GET /compute/api/tasks` in `revocompute/routes.py:4131` currently calls `task_store.list_tasks()`, filters accessible Tasks in Python, sorts and returns **all** summaries. `frontend/src/api/app-api.ts:getTasks()` downloads them all; `frontend/src/features/dashboard/task-query.ts` filters client-side, including a potentially expensive browser regex mode, and ties sort by display name. Therefore a client-only infinite-scroll change **does not** solve network load or complete search semantics. Search must run over the entire authorized collection before limiting returned rows.

## Canonical query contract
Extend `GET /compute/api/tasks` with opt-in `limit` (default bounded 30; hard max 100), opaque `cursor`, `q`, `task_type`, `status`, `owner` (admin-only), `submitted_from/to`, `finished_from/to`, and `sort=submitted|finished`. JSON response `{tasks,next_cursor,has_more,query,totals?}` with explicit server-authoritative filters; no complete list by default. If a legacy client absolutely requires the old all-tasks envelope, provide a separate explicitly bounded compatibility path and document its sunset rather than retaining unbounded default behavior. Reconcile OpenAPI schema and users including MCP/agent/CLI.

Search semantics: case-insensitive **literal substring** of display name and Task ID (and a documented bounded set of additional indexed fields if proven); task type/owner may have their own exact or partial semantics. Do not promise server regex without safe linear-time engine, hard limits and a DB query plan; either remove/disable the current regex UI with an explicit supported-feature explanation or provide a separate validated safe solution. Never evaluate untrusted regex across a huge in-memory Task list. Use indexed SQL queries over the actual persisted Task database; no `list_tasks()` materialization on every page.

## Authorization precedes pagination
Build WHERE scope with the logged-in user id or administrator permission **before** search/sort/limit, preserving deleted-status refusal and all existing visibility constraints. Privileged owner-filter requests must be rejected/ignored for ordinary users without leaking hidden owner identities. Only authorized summaries invoke result/publication access checks, not every Task in the database. Internal query handler must parameterize SQL, bound string lengths, strict ISO UTC dates and normalize invalid page sizes.

## Stable cursor semantics
Use deterministic keyset pagination: for submitted sort, `uploaded_at DESC, task_id DESC`; finished sort uses `finished_at DESC, task_id DESC`, with a documented stable policy for null finishes. Embed/validate page sort key, last timestamp/id, query fingerprint, user/authorization scope and an as-of first-page anchor in a signed opaque cursor with TTL. Reject reuse of a cursor under changed filters, another user or incompatible sort, and supply a restart-from-page-one response. Newer Tasks remain out of an in-progress traversal until refresh; concurrent Task status changes can change filter membership, so **do not falsely promise immutable snapshot semantics** unless backed by a real database snapshot. Define observed-consistency behavior and test same-timestamp ties, deletes, finish transitions and permission changes. Avoid fabricated totals; if an accurate filtered count costs too much, omit it or expose clearly qualified count.

## Browser design
Replace the `getTasks() -> queryTasks(all)` path with typed page fetching. Debounce text search (~250 ms), cancel prior requests with AbortController, reset cursor and selection on filter change, show explicit loading/error/no-match/end markers, and append via IntersectionObserver with accessible Load More fallback. Bound number of DOM cards in memory; use simple windowing only if necessary and preserve keyboard/focus state. Preserve existing mobile filter disclosure, table/compact/detailed view, per-card action authorization, previews and admin filters. Keep bulk selection explicitly scoped to **loaded IDs**, not an accidental 'select all across all pages'. Summary counters must be labeled as returned counts vs full filtered counts.

## Live status is not history retrieval
Do not repeatedly re-fetch the entire page set to update running Tasks. Poll only currently visible non-terminal Task IDs with bounded pacing (or use existing authorized SSE if proven), reconciling status into cards without re-sorting the history query mid-scroll. Separate browse cursor invalidation from live-status refresh. Browser need not fetch page one to become interactive.

## Evidence and operational risk
Unit/DB tests against thousands of Tasks with two users + admin; assertions on SQL-bound number of loaded rows, time/tie pagination and full authorized search. Test unauthorized owner query, deleted Tasks, cursor replay across users/filters, malformed/stale cursor, concurrent inserts/finishes, rate limits, fast typing, slow network, cancellations, duplicate previews and infinite-scroll focus. Compare API wire size and first-interaction latency against current baseline under fixed dataset; screenshots of empty/error/loaded mobile/tablet/desktop states. No schema migration without documented rollback, indexes and explain-plan evidence.

## Non-goals
No Clone & Reuse in this PR (#155), no replacement Task scheduler, no client-only workaround pretending to query all Tasks, no duplicated shadow index. Changelog disposition and independent acceptance mandatory.
